items.title: GPT-5 answered 76% of past finance questions correctly.
items.summary:
GPT-5 answered 76% of past finance questions correctly.

It claimed to know only 38% of them.

This discrepancy is a problem for anyone testing AI on historical market data.

Researchers at The Fin AI created a benchmark to measure this, called FinDendro:
→ 2,226 historical US facts from 1999 to 2026
→ Monthly economic data, end-of-month stock prices, Fed decisions
→ Set up so that random guessing yields a score of about 27%

Results:
→ GPT-5 still correctly answered 61% of the facts it said it didn't know
→ It claimed to know facts up to 7 quarters ago, where its measured knowledge actually ended
→ When the model was told to "answer as of [past date]," it stopped claiming most of what it knew. Its accuracy remained the same.

My take: The model's answer to "Did you know this?" is a poor guide to what it remembers.

This doesn't mean LLMs are bad at forecasting. Backtests aren't reliable for any period the model has already seen.

What this means for you:
If someone shows you an AI that "predicted" the market in 2023, ask one question first: Was 2023 in its training data?

The stated knowledge cutoff won't determine this. Neither will the model's own answer.

items.title: Going beyond frontier capabilities
items.summary:
Going beyond frontier capabilities

Last week, for the first time, we got a step ahead of the AI frontier.

We gave Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1-Sol and GPT-6-Astra the same 12 long-horizon RL tasks and asked them to find the holes.

Our pipeline caught four flaws in AI training tasks that none of them fully caught. Sol and Astra missed 5 more on top of that. 

Three of the four actually sit in security-sensitive code, which is honestly pretty worrying. Train a model on tasks like these and it learns that lax security patterns get rewarded.

How we got here: every flaw our team finds by hand teaches our system what to look for next time. We’ve spent the last few months going deep on exactly one thing, finding what’s broken in AI training data, and it’s starting to compound.

That’s why this matters. Train on a flawed task and you’re paying to teach a model to reward hack. Models are already doing it on their own: just in September, OpenAI reported one of its own agents reward hacking a benchmark to get the answer key.

And if the best public models can’t spot flaws like these, they can’t be relied on to check their own training data either. We believe the same flywheel works anywhere models learn from structured data, and we’ve started talking with robotics and financial data companies about it. Longer term, we want to be for AI training tasks what PSA is for trading cards: a stamp of quality that people trust, backed by an index built on public data (we’re already building this!).

We’re honestly really excited to see where this goes. If you build RL tasks or training data and want to know what’s hiding in it, send us one and we’ll take a look. Looking a little past the horizon is kind of the whole point.

items.title: Artificial Analysis has started benchmarking the search APIs that agents call, not just the models. The latest data is f
items.summary:
Artificial Analysis has started benchmarking the search APIs that agents call, not just the models. The latest data is from November 9.

The setup holds everything else still. One candidate model, GPT-5.6 Luna at medium, one harness, one set of settings. The only thing that changes between runs is which search API the agent uses. The index is the equal-weighted mean of three evaluations. DeepSearchQA F1 over 900 tasks, BrowseComp accuracy on a hard 200-sample subset, and accuracy on a private 600-question set.

The same model with no search at all scores 33. With Keenable Search in pro mode it scores 83. That is the whole case for giving an agent a search tool, in one pair of numbers.

The published table covers 12 products. Keenable pro leads at 83 and Keenable realtime takes 82. Exa auto and Perplexity medium tie at 80, Exa lite and Perplexity high at 79. Octen is 77, Parallel and Brave are 75, OpenAI and https://t.co/Q5R04c4smd are 74, and DeepSeek is 69.

My read. Artificial Analysis splits the bill into search cost and model cost per 1,000 tasks, and the two columns move in opposite directions. Keenable pro costs $31.87 in search and $8.35 in model tokens. DeepSeek costs $8.47 in search and $20.19 in model tokens. Octen is $9.07 and $14.50. So the cheapest search APIs make the model do the most work, at 5 to 7 times the $2.92 the model spends alone. Add the two columns and the ranking changes. Octen lands at $23.57 all in for an index of 77, against $70.34 for Perplexity medium at 80. Three index points for three times the money. A search API's own price tells you very little about what a task costs.

items.title: Pine did 24.3 million views from 1,200 followers. Skyfall did 5 million from 340.
items.summary:
Pine did 24.3 million views from 1,200 followers. Skyfall did 5 million from 340.

Neither post introduced a product. Both opened with a position.

Pine: AI is already smart enough. The problem is the computer. Skyfall: 51 to 125 times faster and 150 to 210 times cheaper than every frontier model tested, GPT-6 Astra included.

The product name comes once, in the last line. The film carries the proof. The copy carries the claim.

Here is why it works. Introducing a product gets liked by people who already follow you. A position gets quoted by strangers who disagree with it. Pine was quoted at 8 times the directory rate in its first hours. Skyfall's numbers were built to be restated in one line: 3.9 seconds and half a cent, against 199 seconds and 75 cents.

The launch post is the last 5 percent of the launch. Both founders had a network quoting with its own take in the first hour. The ranker reads quote velocity as a conversation forming, then distribution widens.

And the bookmark ratio tells you whether anyone intends to try it. Skyfall ran 14,118 bookmarks against 16,377 likes, near one to one. Readers were not agreeing. They were saving it to use.

The rule for your next launch: lead with the claim readers already hold views on. Name the rival you beat. Put the product name once, at the end. Let the demo do the proving.

Introducing your product gets you likes from followers. Taking a position gets you quoted by strangers. Only one of those grows the account.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon went public today. 7 facts most people missed.
items.summary:
Gemini 4 Carbon went public today. 7 facts most people missed.
For long agent jobs I think it is the strongest deal among the top models right now.

Here is why, with the numbers.

1. It makes far fewer confident mistakes than its rivals.
On the Artificial Analysis knowledge test, Carbon's hallucination rate (confident wrong answers) is 11%. Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra are both at 50%. Carbon also had the top score on that test at launch.

2. It handles very long inputs better than anything else in Google's table.
It scored 96.2% on GraphWalks, a test of reasoning over 256K to 1M tokens. Argon got 84.2%. The best non-Google model got 71.8%.

3. It leads the security tests across the whole job.
88.2% on SEC-bench Pro (finding real bugs), 54.8% on ExploitGym (proving a bug can be attacked) and 71.0% on CWE-bench (writing the fix). The ExploitGym gap is the big one, 12 points over GPT-6 Astra. Google says early users already found zero-day bugs (unknown security holes) with it.

4. It is cheaper to run than the models it competes with.
The list price matches Opus 5.5 at $4 in and $20 out per million tokens. Carbon writes 29% fewer output tokens per task, so it costs about 23% less. On SemiAnalysis's GDPx test it scored 10.9% at $16.29 a task. Opus 5.5 scored 12.0% at $51.41 and GPT-6 Astra 9.6% at $53.99.

5. It behaves better as an agent.
→ 0.0% prompt injection success on Gray Swan (hidden instructions inside a page or file)
→ cheating attempts on 0.4% of Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks, none worked
→ overreach (doing more than asked) down 26% from Argon
→ Google says its teams saw it run for days on one engineering task

Scoreboard:

• First on 15 of 17 tests in Google's table
• #1 on the Artificial Analysis index at launch, 9 points above Argon, released two weeks earlier
• #1 on Text Arena (blind votes between models) in early November 2026
• 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, ahead of Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra

Where it is not first:

• GPT-6 Astra wins FrontierSWE 2, 65.5% to 61.2%
• Claude Opus 5.5 wins OSWorld-2.1 (computer use), 87.2% to 81.5%
• Claude Fable 5.2, released 9 November 2026, now leads the Artificial Analysis index with 62 at $9.08 a task and 65 at $26.54. Carbon has 60 at $7.76
• Argon still has a lower hallucination rate, 4% against 11%
• The security scores are Google's own runs with guardrails off

What I find interesting as someone building agents: low hallucination and strong long context are what I want in an agent that reads a lot before it acts. Carbon has both at a price I can run all day. My one doubt is the security scores, since nobody outside Google has rerun them yet.

【MIT系统让机器人超越字面指令进行推理】
MIT和纽约大学的研究人员推出FLEX，让机器人从自然语言指令里推断没有明说的意图。
流程分为三步：添加用户点名的物体，由GPT-4o推断出更宽泛的规则，再使用计算机视觉删除已经不在场的物体。
整个流程大约5秒。
模拟演示里用户输入不要洒到笔记本电脑上，机器人端咖啡的路径同时避开了旁边的手机。
志愿者在端咖啡、移动蜡烛、搬运保龄球三项任务里向模拟机械臂输入指令。
机器人除了执行字面指令，还避开了电子设备、易燃物和易碎物。
研究由MIT助理教授Andreea Bobu主持，将会在本月的Conference on Robot Learning上发表。
我个人的解读是FLEX把常识推断交给了GPT-4o，5秒一轮对家用场景足够快，但是目前只有模拟机械臂和三项任务，搬到真实厨房之前还缺少实机数据。

items.summary:
HPV là loại virus có thể lây cho cả nam và nữ, đặc biệt dễ lây qua tiếp xúc da và niêm mạc khi quan hệ tình dục. Ở nam quan hệ đồng giới, vùng hậu môn là một trong những vị trí HPV tấn công phổ biến nhất, nhưng cũng là nơi nhiều người ngại đi khám nhất vì tâm lý xấu hổ và e ngại bị đánh giá.
Điều đáng nói là HPV thường không gây triệu chứng ngay từ đầu. Ban đầu có thể chỉ là cảm giác ngứa nhẹ, ẩm ướt, nổi vài nốt nhỏ quanh hậu môn hoặc chảy máu nhẹ khi đi vệ sinh. Nhiều người nghĩ mình bị trĩ, viêm da hoặc kích ứng thông thường nên tự mua thuốc bôi mà không đi kiểm tra. Đến khi các nốt sùi phát triển dày hơn, lan rộng hoặc đau rát kéo dài thì mới bắt đầu lo lắng.
Sùi mào gà hậu môn không chỉ ảnh hưởng đến sinh hoạt và tâm lý mà còn có nguy cơ tái phát nhiều lần nếu không theo dõi đúng cách. Một số chủng HPV nguy cơ cao còn liên quan đến ung thư hậu môn nếu nhiễm kéo dài trong nhiều năm. Tuy nhiên, không phải cứ nhiễm HPV là sẽ bị ung thư. Điều quan trọng nhất là phát hiện sớm, theo dõi định kỳ và điều trị đúng phương pháp.
Hiện nay vẫn chưa có thuốc tiêu diệt hoàn toàn HPV trong cơ thể, nhưng y học có nhiều phương pháp giúp kiểm soát tổn thương do virus gây ra như đốt điện, laser, chấm thuốc hoặc tăng cường theo dõi miễn dịch. Bên cạnh đó, tiêm vaccine HPV, quan hệ an toàn và khám sớm khi có dấu hiệu bất thường là những cách rất quan trọng giảm nguy cơ biến chứng. Địa chỉ văn phòng

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution.
